newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Baltic Shipping ready to pay creditors.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Shipping ready to pay creditors.

text.p: Baltic Shipping has set up a group including its biggest shareholders in London to coordinate its debt payments, a company official said on Friday.
Tatyana Chekalova, an aide to Baltic's managing director, told Reuters the company was ready to pay debts to its foreign creditors by selling over 20 ships arrested in foreign ports.
AO Baltiiskoye Morskoye Parokhodstvo owes over $300 million.
"The problem is that the money from selling the ships comes to creditors too slowly and the process must be coordinated and speeded up and this is the aim of the group," she said.
Chekalova also said that Baltic Shipping and its biggest creditor, Germany's Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau, had began talks to restructure $134 million in debt.
She said the credit was taken up under federal government guarantees in the early nineties to buy four ships and now 15 ships were working to repay the debt.
The company's bank accounts are blocked and its employees have not received wages since March.
The government has a 25.5 stake in the company.
Its authorised capital amounts to 3.18 billion roubles.
